reasons: Argument parsing is covered by render-text.test.mjs.
The rendering and text conversion steps have no tests visible in the packet.
The text conversion is crude by design, so its output needs human judgement when used as evidence.

terms.meaning: building the page's HTML on the program's side instead of in the browser
plain HTML with no interactive behaviour attached
a reusable building block of a web page
a code such as an ampersand followed by letters that stands for a special character in HTML
a TypeScript file that also holds page layout code, here the App component

depends_on: frontend/src/App.tsx (the app and its view list)
the tsx runner, which runs TypeScript files without a build step (named in the header)
used_by: The render:text npm script in the frontend folder (named in the header)
frontend/scripts/render-text.test.mjs, which imports its argument parser

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Purpose, imports and startup
sections.what: Explains that the script renders each view to text without a browser, then loads the rendering function, the element builder, and the app with its view list.
sections.why: The header says the same components run as in the browser, so a component that breaks on real data fails here too.
sections.watch_out: The app import loads the whole page, so an error in the app module stops this script before it prints anything.

sections.name: BLOCK, INLINE
sections.title: Tags that start or end a line
sections.what: Two lists: block-level tags such as paragraphs, rows and lists, which end a line, and inline tags such as spans and buttons, which only add a space.
sections.why: The conversion comments say inline spacing matters so that a label and its value do not run together in the output.
sections.watch_out: A tag missing from these lists runs into the text after it, so new kinds of markup may need these lists updated.

sections.name: toText
sections.title: Converting page markup into readable text
sections.what: Turns page markup into plain text: table cells become two spaces, block boundaries become new lines, inline boundaries become one space, a few character codes are decoded, and extra blank lines are removed.
sections.why: The header says the conversion is crude on purpose, because a fuller converter would be a dependency whose bugs would look like rendering bugs.
sections.watch_out: Only a handful of character codes are decoded, so any other special character appears as raw code in the output.

sections.name: parseArgs
sections.title: Reading the command arguments
sections.what: Separates the requested view names from the optional case identifier, so the case value is never mistaken for a view name.
sections.why: The test file and the comments say an earlier bug silently dropped the view name and rendered every view.
sections.watch_out: Any argument starting with two dashes is ignored as a view name, so a typo in a flag is skipped silently rather than reported.

sections.name: main
sections.title: Rendering the chosen views and printing
sections.what: Picks the requested views by exact name, refuses the request if none match and lists the known views, then renders each chosen view to HTML, converts it to text, and prints it under a heading. The script exits with the matching code.
sections.why: The refusal exists so that a mistyped view name produces an error rather than an unexpected full output.
sections.watch_out: If one requested name is valid and another is not, the unknown name is silently ignored and only the valid view prints.

summary: Prints each dashboard view as plain text, rendered from the real components and real generated results, so a view can be read in a terminal or compared in a diff without a browser.
purpose: Lets a person or a tool confirm that the page shows the real data, and provides text for reviews and commit messages.
why: The header says a screenshot proves the layout but this proves the data reached the page, and it uses the same components as the browser so errors show up here too.
how: Parses the requested view names and an optional case identifier. Loads the app and its list of views, renders each chosen view to static HTML, converts that HTML to plain text by turning tags into spaces and line breaks and decoding common character codes, and prints each view under a heading. An unknown view name is refused with a list of the known names. The main routine runs only when the file is started directly, so tests can import it without rendering.
inputs: Command arguments: optional view names, and an optional case flag with a case identifier. The app component and its view list come from frontend/src/App.tsx, which reads the generated bundle.
outputs: Plain text to the terminal with one section per view, each under a heading. Exit code 0 when the views render, and 1 when no requested view name is known.
risks: The HTML-to-text conversion is deliberately crude, so unusual markup may come out wrong, and a bug there can look like a rendering bug. Only what the page shows at render time is captured, so content that appears after a click is missing. The output is text only and cannot show layout.
debug: If a view comes out blank, check that the generated bundle exists and was built from the latest replay. If text looks wrong, print the raw HTML to decide whether the problem is the conversion or the rendering. If the wrong views appear, re-check the argument parsing and its tests.
